Article Title: Para cycling coach pulls out in protest; boccia added
Article Text:
Para cycling chief coach Aditya Mehta

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Boccia gets last-minute clearance

Soaring airfares

NEW DELHI: Para cycling chief coach Aditya Mehta on Wednesday withdrew from the Indian contingent for the Aichi-Nagoya Para Asian Games in protest after eligible cyclists were denied selection. Arshad Shaik is now the lone cyclist to travel to Japan, with only a technician for support.Mehta, who has spent 13 years developing Indian para cycling, said he could not abandon athletes whose “hard-earned opportunities have been taken away”. Mehta will stay back in India while sending Shaik with technician Ramesh Pandi, along with the necessary equipment and technical guidance.“I need to stand by my other athletes, who have worked equally hard but have been denied their opportunity to compete at the Games,” Mehta told TOI, warning that the decision could jeopardise India’s Los Angeles Paralympic qualification prospects.He said India’s Asian rankings — seventh in the men’s category and fourth in the women’s — underline the importance of competing and accumulating points at crucial international events. The actual impact on qualification will depend on the applicable rules and final slot allocation.In a late reprieve, the sports ministry approved two Boccia athletes, Sachin Chamaria and Anjali Devi, for the individual events after initially withholding clearance.Their inclusion takes India’s athlete strength to 168, with 112 men and 56 women competing across 11 disciplines. The overall contingent now stands at 281, including 113 officials.India’s para athletes have also been hit by delayed clearances, triggering a logistical scramble with direct flights to Nagoya no longer available and fares reportedly soaring to five times their usual levels.Athletes now are flying to Tokyo before undertaking a roughly four-hour bus journey to Nagoya, TOIhas learnt. The late bookings leave little time for recovery after the long journey, with some events beginning on Friday.
Article Summary: Para cycling chief coach Aditya Mehta withdraws from the Indian contingent for the Aichi-Nagoya Para Asian Games in protest. Arshad Shaik is now the lone cyclist to travel to Japan, with only a technician for support. Boccia gets last-minute clearance for individual events.

Article Title: Hokato and Soman chase Asian Para Games gold
Article Text:
(From left) Soman Rana with Hokato Hotozhe Sema and coach Rakesh Rawat

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: Nagaland’s Hokato Hotozhe Sema heads into the Para Asian Games carrying both confidence and a touch of uncertainty. The world No. 2 shot putter in the F57 category was in good shape before an injury disrupted his preparations.“It was a minor injury near the hip region. I did the required exercises and it’s fine now. I am confident of achieving my personal best,” said the Paris Paralympics bronze medallist.While he may not have had the smoothest build-up to the Games, 2026 has still been a memorable year for Hokato. The 42-year-old became world No. 1 in his category and also set a national record with a massive throw of 15.21m at the Indian Open Para Athletics Championships in Bengaluru.But Hokato knows that if he is to stand atop the podium, he may have to get past a familiar face: Soman Rana.Ranked world No. 3, 43-year-old Soman Rana arrives at the Asian Para Games as the reigning Commonwealth Games champion and a two-time World Championships silver medallist, having finished runner-up in 2024 and 2025.The pair have trained together at the Army Paralympic Node in Pune since 2017 under coach Rakesh Rawat, developing both a strong friendship and a fierce rivalry.“We’re very close friends. We eat together, train together and spend a lot of time together. Our coordination is excellent,” said Soman, who suffered a mine blast injury while serving with the 2/8 Gorkha Rifles along the Line of Control in Jammu & Kashmir on Dec 1, 2006.For Hokato that friendship comes with an added competitive edge. “There is definitely a lot of competitiveness. We train together and help each other improve, but once competition starts, everyone wants to win,” he said.Rawat believes that rivalry has been one of the biggest reasons behind their development on the international stage.“They motivate each other a great deal,” Rawat said. “Training together gives them valuable experience. They are friends and support each other, but once competition begins, friendship takes a back seat and they become rivals. The one who performs best on the day wins.”The coach expects both throwers to be in contention for medals and insists there is little to separate them. “The rivalry between them has helped both improve. They are very closely matched. On the day, it could go either way,” he said.Soman agrees, although his Commonwealth Games gold is likely to provide an added boost. “The gold gave me a lot of confidence. But I’ve been in this sport for many years. My confidence was already there and winning the medal only strengthened it,” he said.While both athletes believe a podium finish is within reach, neither is willing to predict who will come out on top.For Hokato, however, a gold medal would carry special significance. Since winning bronze in Paris, the road has not been easy. His father passed away last Dec, while he has also been overseeing the construction of a house in his village of P. Vihoto in Nagaland and supporting his daughter, who recently began an MBA programme in Pune.On the field, injuries disrupted his season and forced him to miss the World Para Athletics Grand Prix in New Delhi. Yet, despite the setbacks, Hokato has remained focused on recovery and training.“Recovery is crucial. If you don’t recover properly, there’s no point competing. You can travel all that way and still return empty-handed,” he said.Now, he is eager to return to competition and renew his rivalry with Soman on one of para athletics’ biggest stages. For India, it could be an ideal scenario: two close friends pushing each other every day in training before battling for continental glory when it matters most.
Article Summary: Hokato Hotozhe Sema is the world No. 2 shot putter in the F57 category. Soman Rana is the reigning Commonwealth Games champion. The pair have trained together at the Army Paralympic Node in Pune since 2017.

Article Title: Rakesh Nidagundi designs his destiny from graphics to Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Rakesh Nidagundi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

PUNE: Destiny works in mysterious ways. With his legs affected by polio since childhood, Hubballi’s Rakesh Nidagundi, thought a career in graphic design, would suit him better.Until 2017, he had no idea that it would only open doors to bigger opportunities and a sporting life that he had never thought of.On Wednesday, the Karnataka shooter, 38, will travel to Japan for the Asian Para Games, his first multi-sport event since he started shooting in 2021.“I am very excited and prepared for the Asian Para Games. I have worked hard for this, and I am hoping to do well,” the rifle shooter told TOI. The Karnataka shooter will participate in the 10m air rifle SH1 category at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.Shooting happened to Rakesh by chance. While at his office, he got an order to design a creative publishing material for a shooting academy in Hubballi. “That was the first time I got to know about shooting. The coach at the academy, Ravichandra Balehosur, asked me to visit his academy and try out the sport," Rakesh, who now trains and is sponsored by the Vijayi Bharat Foundation in Ahmedabad, said.“I didn’t think of trying the sport then, but during the Covid-19 lockdown in 2020, I had no work, so I decided to try it once the lockdown was relaxed.I fell in love with the sport and started competing in 2021,” Rakesh said.After he started competing, his life changed after he won medals at the Khelo India Games. “I was supported by the government through the National Centre of Excellence and VBF also came forward to help me. Since then, I have been improving consistently and have won medals at the World level,” said the shooter, who won silver at the World Shooting Para Sport (WSPS) in Changwon, last month.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Defending champion Shailesh Kumar ready for another big jump
Article Text:
Shailesh Kumar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: There was a time when people in his village wondered what future awaited him.Unable to walk properly since childhood after being diagnosed with polio in his right leg, Shailesh Kumar, a resident of Islamnagar village in Bihar’s Jamui district, often faced doubts about what he could achieve.Today, the same people urge him to bring glory to the country, thanks to the success he has achieved in para-athletics. The T63 high jumper heads to the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as the defending champion, carrying not just expectations but also the confidence that comes from changing lives, including his own.“Life has changed significantly, both financially and socially. Earlier, people would wonder what I could achieve because I couldn’t walk properly. Today, their mindset has changed. They see that a para athlete can represent the country and achieve success,” Shailesh told TOI ahead of the Games.Since winning gold with a Games record at the 2023 Asian Para Games in China, the 26-year-old has added several major titles to his résumé, including gold medals at 2025 World Para Athletics Championships and 2026 World Para Athletics Grand Prix.Training under close friend and coach Ronak Malik in Bengaluru since Jan 2025, the 26-year-old is now focused on defending his high jump title.He enters the competition after overcoming knee issues that troubled him earlier in the season, but Malik is confident his ward can retain the gold medal in high jump and also contend for a podium finish in long jump.“If everything goes according to plan, he has the potential to win medals in both events. Gold is definitely a possibility. He has already set records at the World Championships and Asian Championships and has achieved personal best performances,” said Malik, a former national-level high jumper.Training a para athlete requires a different approach from coaching able-bodied athletes, and Malik regularly consults experienced jump coach GV Gaonkar to fine-tune Shailesh’s programme.While Malik’s guidance has proved hugely beneficial on the field, their friendship has also played a key role in Shailesh’s resurgence, particularly after Paris Paralympics, where he narrowly missed a medal and finished fourth.“After beginning his training in Sonipat in 2019, Shailesh moved to SAI Gandhinagar under coach Vinod Chauhan. Unfortunately, Vinod sir passed away in a road accident in April 2023. It was a difficult phase for Shailesh and he wasn’t in the best frame of mind going into the Paris Paralympics,” Malik said.It was after Chauhan’s death that Shailesh reconnected with Malik. Together, they are now targeting success not only at the Asian Para Games but also at next year’s World Championships and, ultimately, the Paralympics in LA.But as Malik says, none of it would have been possible without the discipline and dedication of Shailesh, who chose sport even as his family hoped he would focus on studies and secure a stable job.“People had different opinions about me, so I wanted to do something different. My family stood by me throughout and today they are very proud,” said Shailesh.But as he prepares for another Asian Para Games campaign, he remains determined not to be weighed down by expectations. “I am the defending champion, but I am an athlete first. When you represent the country there is pressure, but I try to keep it to a minimum and perform freely,” he said.For Shailesh, though, the biggest motivation remains the journey itself. From being doubted because of his disability to becoming a champion who inspires others, he believes para-sports have given him a life he never imagined, and he intends to make the most of it.
Article Summary: Shailesh Kumar is the defending champion of the T63 high jump at the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. The 26-year-old was diagnosed with polio in his right leg as a child. He has won several major titles, including gold medals at 2025 World Para Athletics Championships and 2026 World ParA Athletics Grand Prix.

Article Title: Ban threat on para shooters for challenging PCI in court
Article Text:
Imag credit: X

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With India’s Asian Para Games preparations already marred by selection disputes and court battles, the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) has landed in another controversy over a para shooting policy that threatens athletes with lengthy bans for challenging its decisions in court.A clause in the PCI governing body-approved 2026-27 national selection policy for para shooting prescribes a three-year ban if a shooter or their parents initiate legal action against the association and the case is dismissed. A repeat offence could invite a lifetime ban, according to the 16-page policy, a copy of which is with TOI.“Any para shooters/coaches/parents going to the courts or taking any legal action against the association and further if the case is dismissed by the court, the para shooter would be banned for at least three years and in case of repeated offence, ban could go for lifetime as well,” the clause states.The provision raises questions about athletes’ right to seek judicial redress in selection disputes, potentially exposing para shooters to severe sporting sanctions for challenging the PCI’s decisions.A senior PCI official told TOI that the clause was damaging and should never have been included. The official said directions had been issued to amend the policy and that a corrigendum would be uploaded. However, since the policy was approved by the governing body, a formal amendment may be necessary.It is learnt that some shooters unhappy with their exclusion from the Asian Para Games squad refrained from approaching the courts for fear of being banned.Boccia dropped, contingent shrinks to 10 sportsThe controversy comes amid further reductions in India’s contingent for the Games. After para fencing, boccia has become the latest discipline to be dropped, with the sports ministry withholding clearance for the two-member team of Sachin Chamaria and Anjali Devi.India, initially scheduled to compete in 12 sports, will now participate in 10. The ministry cleared 166 athletes late Monday evening, taking the delegation’s strength to 275, including 94 team officials and support staff and 15 contingent staff. The Games begin in Nagoya on Oct 18.Para athletics accounts for the largest share of the contingent, with 62 athletes, including 46 men, along with 36 support staff.Para shooting chief coach JP Nautiyal has not received clearance despite representations from nine of the 13 selected shooters. Jeevan L Rai and Rakesh Singh will oversee the team. Nautiyal has faced allegations of violating selection criteria and demanding kickbacks.Cyclists’ hopes end with DRMThe final Delegation Registration Meeting (DRM) in Nagoya on Monday has effectively closed the door on additional entries. Para cyclists awaiting court relief against their exclusion will miss the Games even if they secure a favourable order later.Only Arshad Shaik will compete, while six other cyclists selected by the Cycling Federation of India and the PCI were omitted for allegedly failing to meet the prescribed criteria.Baretha questions Suhas’ inclusionPara badminton player Chirag Baretha has questioned the last-minute inclusion of LY Suhas, citing his absence from national and international competition since the Paris Paralympics in 2024.Baretha, a two-time Asian Para Games medallist, was excluded after the ministry ruled that he did not meet the selection criteria.“How a player can be qualified and sanctioned in the events at the Asian Para Games, he has never played a single game in the events he is qualified. Arbitration in sports can be visibly seen with the sanction issued for upcoming Games,” Baretha wrote on X.Manisha Patel, Shashank Kumar, Ammu Beulah Mohan and Rachna Patel were also denied clearance by the ministry.
Article Summary: PCI threatens athletes with lengthy bans for challenging its decisions in court. Clause in 2026-27 national selection policy for para shooting prescribes three- year ban if a shooter or their parents initiate legal action against the association. A repeat offence could invite a lifetime ban, according to the 16-page policy.

Article Title: Para-shooters allege corruption in Asian Games selection; PCI chief says process ‘100% fair’
Article Text:

Sandeep Kumar alleges selection bias

PCI rejects all allegations

Ministry says grievances will be examined

The selection of India’s para-shooting team for the Aichi-Nagoya Para Asian Games has come under a cloud of controversy after a group of para-shooters alleged corruption and financial demands in the selection process.The shooters have sought an independent inquiry into what they described as financial corruption, extortion and manipulation by officials of the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) and its Shooting Technical Committee (STC).In a representation submitted to the Director General of the Sports Authority of India (SAI) on Wednesday, the athletes alleged “illicit monetary extortion”, “brazen corruption” and violations of Sports Ministry guidelines.The Para Asian Games are scheduled to be held from October 18 to 24.One of the most serious allegations made in the representation was that athletes were being asked to give 20 per cent of their government cash awards as a condition for being selected for the national team.“Athletes are being coerced under severe duress into paying an illegal kickback of 20 per cent of their sanctioned government cash awards to designated committee office-bearers as a mandatory pre-condition for national team selection,” the representation alleged.The shooters also alleged that international quota places were not allocated purely on rankings and performances. They claimed financial considerations played a role in deciding who received the available places.According to their representation, two of the 15 international quota places available to India were surrendered because athletes next in line allegedly refused to meet the financial demands. The athletes also accused the selection committee of changing qualifying scores, ignoring Sports Ministry criteria and replacing an earlier selection panel without giving a recorded reason.P4 50m free pistol SH1 shooter Sandeep Kumar, ranked third in Asia, also questioned the selection decisions. He alleged that Rudrankksh Khandelwal, ranked 14th in Asia, was picked ahead of Akash, the Asian No. 1, and himself. Sandeep said he was “deeply aggrieved” by what he described as arbitrary decisions and violations of the selection rules.The shooters also questioned the appointment of an individual as a technical expert and Director of Operations, alleging that the person had no record of competing in an official shooting event.PCI president Devendra Jhajharia strongly rejected the charges and said the team had been selected strictly according to the prescribed rules.“The selection has been done as per the criteria. There has been no discrimination against anyone. The selections are 100 per cent fair and according to the Sports Ministry’s guidelines,” Jhajharia, a two-time Paralympics javelin gold-medallist, told PTI.Jhajharia also rejected Sandeep’s allegation that he was left out to make way for a shooter who had links with the coach.“Those are all false allegations,” Jhajharia said.A Sports Ministry source said genuine complaints raised by the para-shooters would be looked into. However, the source added that the Indian team for the Para Asian Games had already been finalised and could not be changed at this stage.The shooters have also indicated that they could take the matter to court if their allegations are not addressed.They said they may approach the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution, seeking a writ of mandamus and a court-monitored investigation into the selection process.
Article Summary: Shooters seek independent inquiry into what they described as financial corruption, extortion and manipulation by officials of the Paralympic Committee of India. Two of the 15 international quota places available to India were surrendered because athletes next in line allegedly refused to meet the financial demands. The athletes also accused the selection committee of changing qualifying scores and ignoring Sports Ministry criteria.

Article Title: ‘Carrying the tricolour is a different feeling’: Pramod Bhagat eyes gold at Para Asian Games

NEW DELHI: For a champion who has conquered the biggest stages in para badminton, the prospect of carrying the Indian flag as the flagbearer at the upcoming Para Asian Games for Pramod Bhagat is still an experience that stands apart from every medal and accolade.A gold medallist at the Tokyo Paralympics, Bhagat is preparing for his fifth Asian Para Games, carrying with him the experience of six medals, including two golds and four bronze. Yet, despite years of competing at the highest level, the responsibility of carrying the tricolour has brought a fresh sense of excitement.Bhagat recalled watching flag bearers lead the Indian contingent during his earlier appearances at the continental showpiece. The sight left a lasting impression on him, and now, as he prepares to take on that role himself, the feeling has become all the more meaningful.Having already won Paralympic gold, two Asian Games gold medals and the Padma Shri, Bhagat has experienced several defining moments in his sporting journey. However, he believes that the honour of being flag bearer cannot be compared with any of those achievements.“My expectation is gold, but it won't be easy,” he said, underlining the ambition that continues to drive him despite an already impressive medal collection.For Bhagat, longevity at the highest level has been built on the ability to adapt. Every edition of the Asian Para Games brings a different set of challenges, with opponents improving, preparations changing and the demands of the sport becoming more intense.“When you go to the second or third Asian Para Games, there is a difference of four years. A lot changes in four years. I try to learn from the past and move forward. I try to do my best, and I want to be successful,” he said.That approach has helped Bhagat remain a key figure in India's para badminton movement. His focus is not simply on defending his reputation but on finding ways to improve with every campaign. The target remains gold, but the process involves learning from previous performances, understanding the competition and making the most of his preparation.Beyond his personal ambitions, Bhagat is equally encouraged by the growing strength of Indian para badminton. With the sport attracting greater attention and Indian athletes making their presence felt internationally, expectations have risen.The goal, he said, is to push the country's medal count even higher.“We want to win more than 10 medals in the Para Asian Games,” Bhagat said, reflecting the confidence within the Indian contingent.The optimism is backed by a broader upward trend in India's para-sports performance. Bhagat pointed to the country's growing medal tally, noting that India had crossed the 100-medal mark at the previous Asian Para Games. For him, the progress is evidence of how sustained support, improved facilities and greater visibility can translate into results on the field.He believes the transformation has been particularly noticeable compared with the early days of his career, when govt assistance and public recognition for para badminton were more limited.Bhagat credited the government's growing involvement and thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for taking a personal interest in para badminton, which he said had helped bring the sport greater recognition and publicity. That visibility, in turn, encouraged private organisations to come forward and support athletes.“When you get good support, and your equipment and training facilities improve, you perform well,” he said.The backing from both the government and the private sector, Bhagat believes, has helped create a stronger ecosystem for para athletes. Better equipment, improved training infrastructure and greater exposure have given players more opportunities to prepare and compete at the highest level. The rising medal count, he said, reflects the difference that such support can make.As India looks to build on its achievements at the continental level, Bhagat's campaign carries significance beyond the medals he hopes to win. He represents a generation of athletes who have benefited from a changing sporting environment while helping raise the profile of para badminton through their performances.For the veteran shuttler, though, the immediate task remains clear: prepare well, learn from experience and pursue gold. The flag-bearing honour has added another dimension to his campaign, giving him a responsibility that goes beyond his individual events.Bhagat knows that success will not come easily, but he is ready to embrace the challenge. And when he leads the Indian contingent with the tricolour in his hands, the moment will represent more than the achievements of a champion. It will reflect the journey of Indian para badminton, the progress of its athletes and the pride of representing the country.

Article Title: Para cyclists’ protest enters Day 2, even sole Asian Para Games pick joins stir

NEW DELHI: With the Asian Para Games fast approaching, India’s para cyclists are spending their days demanding answers instead of focusing on their preparations, as their protest against the team selection entered its second consecutive day on Friday.The cyclists continued their sit-in outside Gate No. 1 of Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) stadium, braving the harsh sun and sitting on the pavement to demand justice and the inclusion of the athletes they say were overlooked despite meeting the selection criteria. Their grievance remains unchanged: six cyclists were recommended by the joint selection committee of the Cycling Federation of India (CFI) and Paralympic Committee of India (PCI), but only one — Arshad Shaikh — made the final contingent for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games.Even Shaikh, the lone cyclist selected, has joined the protest in solidarity with his fellow athletes. Instead of concentrating solely on his training and preparations for the continental event, he is standing alongside those questioning why they were left out.The athletes allege that their repeated appeals have failed to elicit a satisfactory response from the authorities. They want the selection decision reconsidered and a clear explanation of why the other recommended cyclists were excluded.The protesters say they will continue their agitation until their demands are met and the sidelined athletes are considered for selection.The dispute stems from the joint selection committee’s August 28 meeting, at which six cyclists were unanimously recommended for the Games. The list comprised Shaikh (MC2), Pavan Kumar Kommoji (MC3), Sameer (MC4), Prashant Arkal (MH4), Vishva Vasani (WC3) and Lisha Das (WC4).According to the athletes, their recommendations were based on performances, minimum qualifying standards, Asian and Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) rankings, and international qualification criteria. They have sought athlete-wise explanations and clarity on the basis on which the final list was reduced from six names to one.The cyclists have also pointed to the financial burden they have borne, claiming to have met expenses related to international participation, equipment and prosthetics themselves. With the Games looming, they argue that the uncertainty over their selection has added to the strain on athletes who should be preparing to represent the country.The Asian rankings cited by the athletes show that several of the excluded cyclists had competitive positions in their respective categories. In 2026, Shaikh was ranked second in road and third in track, while Kommoji was second and third, respectively. Sameer was eighth in road and fifth in track; Arkal was second in road; Vasani was third in road and second in track; and Das was sixth in road and second in track. Track rankings do not apply to the MH4 category.The athletes have also cited India’s position in the Asian UCI Nations Rankings as part of their argument over qualification slots, seeking transparency on how the available places were allocated.The cyclists’ protest comes amid wider discontent over selections for the Asian Para Games. Para-shooters have also continued to raise objections over the selection process. On Thursday, their protest at the Indian contingent’s send-off ceremony brought allegations of irregularities and favouritism into focus, with athletes questioning their exclusion from the squad. The allegations have been contested by officials, who have maintained that selection was based on the prescribed criteria.With both groups raising concerns over selection transparency, the protests have cast a shadow over India’s preparations for the Games. For the cyclists outside JLN stadium, however, the immediate demand remains simple: an explanation for the decision, a fair hearing and a resolution before the team departs for Japan.“We will continue our protest until our demands are met,” the cyclists have maintained.For athletes who should be sharpening their competitive edge ahead of a major international event, the question now is how long they will have to remain on the pavement before their pleas are heard.
Article Summary: The cyclists continued their sit-in outside Gate No. 1 of Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) stadium. Six cyclists were recommended by the joint selection committee of the Cycling Federation of India (CFI) and Paralympic Committee of India. Only one — Arshad Shaikh — made the final contingent for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games.

The UAE has spent years attracting some of football’s biggest names, but its Golden Visa programme offers more than a convenient way for global stars to visit the Emirates. Since the government expanded eligibility to exceptional sporting talent in 2020, footballers have used their connections with the country in different ways, from establishing businesses and investing in local football to building media ventures and developing opportunities for young players. Here are 10 footballers who received the coveted residency, and what their relationships with the UAE have looked like beyond the initial announcements.The UAE introduced its Golden Residency programme in 2019 under an initiative announced by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, the country’s Vice-President and Prime Minister and Dubai’s ruler. Initially associated with investors, entrepreneurs and specialised professionals, the programme offered eligible foreign nationals a longer-term alternative to conventional residence permits tied to employment or local sponsorship.A significant expansion followed in 2020, when the UAE Cabinet extended the 10-year residency pathway to exceptional sporting talent. The Dubai Sports Council helped bring prominent international athletes into the programme, with Cristiano Ronaldo and several other football stars forming part of the first sporting cohort.The change reflected an ambition extending beyond attracting famous visitors. Under the UAE’s economic diversification strategy, including the longer-term objectives associated with We the UAE 2031 and Dubai’s D33 Economic Agenda, global talent can help strengthen industries beyond oil, including technology, tourism, healthcare, education and professional sport.Footballers offer a particularly visible connection between those ambitions and the wider public. Their international audiences can bring attention to local sporting facilities, youth development programmes, commercial partnerships and investment opportunities, while some recipients have gone on to establish more direct professional or business ties with the country.The Golden Visa is a renewable, long-term residency permit that allows eligible foreign nationals to live, work, study and invest in the UAE without requiring an employer or another local sponsor to maintain their residency. Depending on the applicable category and eligibility conditions, the permit can last five or 10 years.Its main benefits include:Following the expansion, the programme now covers several categories, including property investors, entrepreneurs, scientists, skilled professionals, outstanding students and graduates, humanitarian pioneers, and exceptional talents in sport, culture and the arts. Each pathway has its own criteria and application or nomination process, so receiving the visa does not necessarily require buying property or taking up employment with a UAE-based organisation.For footballers, the expanded sporting category created a route to long-term residency based on exceptional achievement and talent, rather than requiring them to leave their existing clubs and move to the Emirates.Portuguese forward Cristiano Ronaldo received his 10-year UAE Golden Visa in February 2020 while playing for Juventus, becoming one of the most prominent beneficiaries of the newly expanded sporting category. The recognition followed his sixth Best Men's Player accolade at the Dubai Globe Soccer Awards on 29 December 2019, reflecting both his international standing and his established relationship with the Emirate.His placement in the inaugural sporting cohort demonstrated that an athlete could maintain an active career abroad while holding long-term UAE residency. Ronaldo subsequently signed with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia in January 2023, extending his commitment through June 2027, while frequently visiting Dubai for personal and professional obligations. To anchor this long-term connection to the region, Ronaldo expanded his international real estate portfolio by acquiring a €25 million plot of land on Jumeirah Bay Island—a highly exclusive, seahorse-shaped enclave widely known as "Billionaire Island". The acquisition was made to construct a custom waterfront mega-mansion, providing a permanent family base in the UAE just a short distance from his football commitments in Riyadh.His relationship with the Emirates also features a prominent personal dimension, highlighted by a well-documented friendship with the Crown Prince of Dubai, Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum. Ronaldo has repeatedly spoken warmly of the city, stating during an appearance at Expo 2020 Dubai on 28 January 2022: “I thank all my fans... I love Dubai, its culture and its people, and I visit Dubai every year, and I am very happy to be here. ”Former Chelsea and Ivory Coast striker Didier Drogba received his Golden Visa in November 2020, when Major General Mohammad Ahmad Al Marri, director of Dubai’s General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs, welcomed him at the department’s headquarters to present the residency card.The recognition came after a decorated career that included four English Premier League titles and a Champions League crown with Chelsea. Drogba was also presented with thein appreciation of his support for the Dubai Sports Council’scampaign, which encouraged residents to prioritise physical wellbeing during the pandemic.His connection with Dubai extended beyond football, with the former striker exploring opportunities involving commercial property, sports academies and the wider sports sector. He has also participated in international business events, including AIBC Eurasia, bringing his sporting profile into discussions around emerging technology, blockchain and investment.Brazilian World Cup winner Ronaldinho, whose full name is Ronaldo de Assis Moreira, received his 10-year Golden Visa in May 2021 through Dubai’s General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs. Major General Mohammed Al Marri and his deputy, Major General Obaid Muhair bin Surour, were present when the former Barcelona and AC Milan playmaker received the residency.Ronaldinho’s relationship with the UAE has included ambitions around youth football and wider sporting partnerships. He signed a strategic memorandum of understanding with Abu Dhabi-based Palms Sports, establishing a framework intended to combine elite athletic development with academic opportunities for young Emirati athletes.He has also laid the groundwork for ain Dubai, with the proposed project centred on structured coaching and the Brazilian approach to attacking football commonly associated with. His wider appearances across the region have included sports events, corporate gatherings and digital-technology exhibitions, where his global profile attracts audiences beyond traditional football supporters.Ronaldinho has regularly visited and trained in Dubai since his youth, making the city a familiar base for his regional engagements. His Golden Visa provides long-term residency flexibility while he explores sporting, commercial and cultural opportunities across the Emirates.French midfielder and World Cup winner Paul Pogba was among the elite sporting figures granted a UAE Golden Visa in February 2020. At the time, the former Manchester United star had already established a strong connection with Dubai, regularly utilizing the city's sports infrastructure for off-season conditioning and warm-weather training.Dubai’s high-performance training centres have been central to Pogba’s conditioning and rehabilitation, particularly at Nad Al Sheba Sports Complex and Transform Altitude Performance Center. He has also supported local fitness campaigns with the Dubai Sports Council and mentored young players at community events.His regional interests have since expanded beyond football into traditional Gulf sports culture. In late 2025, Pogba became a significant shareholder and global ambassador for Al Haboob, the world’s first professional camel racing team. The Saudi-founded organization competes heavily across the UAE and the wider Gulf region, aiming to modernize the sport by introducing advanced sports science, data tracking, and robotic jockey technology. Pogba’s involvement is intended to help elevate camel racing to a global audience, bridging the gap between historical heritage and modern professional sports management.Belgian striker Romelu Lukaku was another big name from that initial wave of sports stars to secure a UAE Golden Visa in February 2020, right while he was dominating Serie A with Inter Milan. The long-term residency was a massive nod to his status as one of Europe’s top forwards, giving him a permanent tie to the Emirates without having to uproot his club career.Lukaku’s Dubai connection grew at the 14th Dubai International Sports Conference, where he joined João Félix and Mikael Silvestre to discuss football technology. He also spoke about coping with online racism, urging young players to use social media positively. The event ended with a viral moment when a UAE royal presented him with a golden plaque that misspelled his name as “Romello”.When he isn’t speaking at summits, Lukaku uses Dubai as his ultimate reset button. He’s a regular at the world-class Nad Al Sheba Sports Complex during league winter breaks, using the warm weather and high-tech facilities to keep his conditioning at an elite level. His routine fits perfectly into Dubai's push to become the global capital for off-season athletic recovery.Former Portugal international Luís Figo, the 2000 Ballon d’Or winner who played for Barcelona, Real Madrid and Inter Milan, received his Golden Visa as part of the February 2020 sporting initiative. The residency recognised his career at the highest level while giving him a long-term base for professional and commercial activities across the region.Figo has maintained links with Dubai through brand partnerships and sporting events, including collaborations with Mastercard Middle East and Africa during Expo 2020 Dubai. His appearances included fan meet-and-greet sessions and promotional activities featuring the UEFA Champions League trophy.He also participated in a Guinness World Record initiative involving the highest-altitude football match played on a parabolic flight, a campaign coordinated through Dubai. Alongside those commercial engagements, Figo supported the Dubai Sports Council’s Be Fit, Be Safe campaign during the pandemic, encouraging residents to remain physically active while public spaces were restricted.His post-playing career has increasingly involved ambassadorial work and international business events, making the Golden Visa a useful foundation for maintaining commitments across Europe and the Middle East.Brazilian World Cup winner and former Real Madrid left-back Roberto Carlos received his Golden Visa in February 2020, joining a group of football legends recognised for their sporting achievements and connections with the Emirates. His relationship with Dubai has included exhibition matches, community fitness initiatives and youth football development.In August 2026, Carlos became a co-owner and shareholder of Dubai-based Fursan Hispania FC, alongside former footballers Michel Salgado and Fernando Hierro. The club’s youth development ambitions offer him a more direct role in the local game, using international football connections and technical experience to help develop young players and create pathways towards professional opportunities in Europe.Carlos has also supported the Real Madrid Foundation’s work in the UAE through a partnership with ISD Sports City, helping launch an educational football programme at the ISD La Liga Academy campus. The initiative provides training for more than 1,000 young footballers.His work also includes youth clinics and appearances promoting Real Madrid World at Dubai Parks and Resorts, extending his involvement from football development into the UAE’s sports tourism sector.Bosnian midfielder Miralem Pjanić received his Golden Visa in February 2020 while playing for Juventus, becoming one of the active European footballers included in the programme’s first sporting cohort. His subsequent career gave him a particularly direct connection with the Emirates when he left Barcelona in September 2022 to join Sharjah FC.Unlike recipients whose UAE relationships have centred mainly on visits and commercial appearances, Pjanić played in the UAE Pro League for two seasons between 2022 and 2024. His experience at Juventus and Barcelona brought elite European experience into the domestic competition, and he helped Sharjah win the UAE President’s Cup and the UAE League Cup.During his time in the country, Pjanić also had opportunities to mentor younger domestic players, sharing experience from years competing at the highest levels of European football. Following his UAE spell and later playing career, he maintained ties with Dubai and became involved with Mundial Football Academy, a venture focused on identifying and training grassroots talent using high-performance football methods.Former Manchester United and England captain Rio Ferdinand transitioned to a permanent life in the UAE in August 2025, relocating his family to a £6.5 million mansion in Dubai's luxury Al Barari community. This move followed his departure from his prominent UK punditry role at TNT Sports in May 2025. While he enjoyed a long-standing relationship with the region, this relocation marked the formal establishment of Dubai as the central base for his media work, business interests, and 10-year UAE Golden Visa residency framework.Ferdinand has since actively scaled his digital media platform, Rio Presents, while anchoring himself in the UAE’s expanding creator economy. He was featured as a prominent fireside speaker at Dubai’s 1 Billion Followers Summit, where he discussed the future of digital media and how modern creators can build sustainable international audiences independently of traditional television.Beyond media, his regional business activities extend into real estate through strategic partnerships with prominent firms like LEOS Developments. In the sports and tourism sector, he co-operates Football Escapes, a premium holiday football coaching concept that organizes youth camps led by UEFA-licensed former professionals at luxury resorts.Ferdinand and his wife, Kate, also engage with the local community through public wellness initiatives, including fitness events hosted at Jumeirah Beach near the Burj Al Arab.Former Manchester United champion and French national team captain Patrice Evra was awarded his UAE Golden Visa back in 2021 under the exceptional-talent framework. . Since then, he has fully leaned into the local lifestyle, famously calling Dubai his "home sweet home" and basing himself out of a luxury penthouse on the Palm Jumeirah.Instead of just enjoying retirement, Evra has used his long-term visa to pivot into a serious second career as a Dubai-based entrepreneur. He has set up several companies in the UAE covering everything from beauty and fitness to deep tech. In fact, while speaking at regional business events like the Invest in Sharjah forum and Token2049 Dubai, he pointed out just how much of a game-changer the region's geography is for a global business. He noted that with nearly two-thirds of the world’s population sitting within an eight-hour flight, running a global empire from Dubai feels a world away from his old days managing companies in the UK, where he felt entirely isolated from fast-growing markets like Asia.Lately, Evra has been bridging the gap between real estate and sports technology. He officially partnered with UAE developer Major Developments as a core project partner for Colibri Views, a massive new high-rise project at RAK Central in Ras Al Khaimah. Evra actually designed the crown jewel of the tower himself: the UAE's very first rooftop Footbot simulator. It’s an AI-driven, high-tech football arena packed with smart motion sensors and performance tracking to help residents train like elite pros.On top of the commercial tech, he is also focused on grassroots football through his Dubai-based project, Love This Game FC. The whole idea is to scout and train young local talent in the UAE, giving them a real pathway to score professional trials over in Europe and the UK.
Article Summary: The UAE introduced its Golden Residency programme in 2019. It offers long-term residency, providing greater continuity than shorter-term permits. Holders can sponsor spouses, children regardless of age and parents. They can pursue eligible professional, educational and commercial activities within the UAE. Here are 10 footballers who received the coveted residency.

Article Title: Real Madrid become first club in sports history to record €1.22bn in revenue in 2025-26 despite trophyless season: How did they pull it off?
Article Text:
Real Madrid generated a record €1.221 billion in 2025-26 despite a trophyless season, an ambitious Bernabéu renovation and hefty spending on star players.

Real Madrid's record revenue comes with one important footnote

Pope Leo XIV meets with Real Madrid president Florentino Perez, during a meeting with the diocesan community at the Santiago Bernabeu Stadium, in Madrid, Spain, June 8, 2026. Elisabetta Trevisan/Vatican Media/­Handout via REUTERS ATTENTION EDITORS - THIS IMAGE WAS PROVIDED BY A THIRD PARTY.

The Bernabéu has become a major revenue engine, but the rebuild remains expensive

FILE - Workers prepare the field at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium ahead of an NFL game between the Miami Dolphins and Washington Commanders in Madrid, Spain, Friday, Nov. 14, 2025. (AP Photo/Steve Luciano, File)

Pope Leo XIV arrives on the occasion of a meeting with the diocesan community at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium in Madrid, Spain, Monday, June 8, 2026. (AP Photo/Bernat Armangue)

Adidas, Emirates and HP help push commercial income higher

Madrid are spending heavily on the squad without losing sight of sustainability

The Real Madrid Foundation extends the club's reach beyond football

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Real Madrid finished the 2025-26 season without a major trophy, but their finances tell a very different story. The club generated €1.221 billion ($1.42 billion) in operating revenue, becoming the first organisation in sports history to cross the €1.2 billion mark. The record comes despite an ambitious renovation of the Santiago Bernabéu, hefty investments in star players and a trophyless campaign. So, how did Madrid manage to reach a financial milestone no other sports organisation has achieved, and what role did the revamped stadium, lucrative sponsorships and their expanding commercial business play?Real Madrid's board approved the accounts for the 2025-26 financial year on July 28, 2026, reporting operating revenue of €1,221.3 million ($1.42 billion), an increase of 3.1% from the previous year and the club's third consecutive annual revenue record.The achievement is substantial, particularly because the club reached it without winning a major trophy during the season. Real Madrid's operating revenue excludes player transfer fees, distinguishing the figure from financial measures that include income generated by selling footballers.However, there is an accounting detail worth understanding before celebrating the milestone. The published total includes €23.5 million ($27.3 million) recognised through the reversal of a financial provision linked to a European Commission case settled the previous year. Removing that amount would bring operating revenue to approximately €1.198 billion ($1.39 billion), just below the historic threshold, although Madrid would still rank comfortably among the world's highest-earning sporting organisationsThe club also reported record earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation of €287 million ($333.4 million), an 18% rise year on year.Three principal businesses account for most of the reported revenue: marketing and commercial activities, stadium operations, and broadcasting and competitions. Together, they show how Madrid have built a financial model capable of generating enormous income even when trophies do not arrive.The renovated Santiago Bernabéu contributed €363 million ($421.7 million) during 2025-26, an 11% increase from the previous season and more than double the stadium income generated before redevelopment.Matchday operations, premium hospitality, stadium experiences and personal seat licences have helped expand the venue's earning potential. These licences give supporters the right to purchase season tickets over the next three decades, allowing Madrid to generate income from a long-term relationship with their customers rather than relying exclusively on individual match sales.The redevelopment has also transformed the stadium itself through features including a retractable roof, a 360-degree video scoreboard and an underground pitch-storage system that preserves sections of the playing surface when the venue hosts other events. These engineering projects, alongside luxury catering facilities and other finishing touches, have contributed to the renovation's cumulative cost reaching €1.407 billion ($1.63 billion) by the end of 2025-26, compared with an original plan valued at €575 million ($667.9 million) in 2018.Madrid spent a €184 million ($213.7 million) completing work during the latest financial year, including mandatory soundproofing upgrades. Major music concerts have remained suspended since late 2024 following neighbourhood noise complaints and restrictions requiring sound levels to remain within a 55-decibel limit, forcing planned performances by artists including Aitana and Lola Índigo to move to alternative venues.The club has also faced a setback over two proposed nearby parking facilities after Spain's Supreme Court blocked the plans, removing another potential source of long-term stadium income. Madrid officials have played down the financial consequences, maintaining that the parking project would not materially alter the club's overall position.The stadium's financing nevertheless remains substantial, with approximately €1.1 billion ($1.28 billion) in outstanding project debt carried through three long-term, fixed-interest loans taken out in 2019, 2021 and 2023. Madrid accounts for that financing separately from its ordinary operating position, which leaves reported day-to-day net debt at approximately €9 million ($10.5 million).With an annual debt repayment of around €60 million ($69.7 million), the stadium must keep producing substantial returns, even as Madrid expect its modernised facilities to remain more profitable than the old ground.Marketing revenue reached €539 million ($626.1 million) in 2025-26, representing a 6% annual increase and growth of approximately 82% against the club's pre-renovation 2018-19 baseline.The sponsorship portfolio is anchored by three prominent agreements that together are estimated to generate between €290 million and €300 million ($337.1 million-$348.7 million) annually. Adidas supplies the kit under a deal worth approximately €120 million ($139.4 million) per year, while Emirates pays an estimated €100 million ($116.2 million) annually as the principal shirt sponsor and HP contributes an estimated €70 million to €80 million ($81.5 million-$92.9 million) through its sleeve partnership.The timing of the renewals has strengthened that commercial foundation. Emirates extended its agreement on June 9, 2026, securing the front of the shirt through 2031, while Adidas renewed its kit partnership on June 10, extending the relationship until 2034. HP's multi-year agreement, signed on February 2, 2024, marked the first time in Madrid's 121-year history that a sponsor's logo appeared on the playing shirt's sleeve.The remaining marketing income comes from global merchandising and licensing, estimated at €140 million to €150 million ($162.6 million-$174.3 million), and another €90 million to €110 million ($104.5 million-$127.8 million) from regional and secondary partners.Official shirts, training equipment, the Bernabéu megastore, online sales and more than 30 corporate partners help Madrid make money from their global popularity beyond the weekly television audience. That commercial reach has become increasingly important as the club looks to maximise the value of its brand independently of results on the pitch.The revenue record has not stopped Madrid from investing in the team and its infrastructure. The club allocated €161 million ($187.1 million) directly to new player signings during 2025-26, while overall sports staff expenses, including wages and the annual accounting cost of transfer fees, increased from €540 million ($627.2 million) in 2018-19 to €618 million ($717.8 million)Despite that increase, player wages and transfer amortisation represented approximately 46% of total revenue, remaining below the 50% threshold the club identifies as a useful benchmark for financial discipline. Madrid also invested €192 million ($222.9 million) in facilities, technology and infrastructure during the financial year, reinforcing the spending commitment beyond the senior squad.As a member-owned club, Madrid does not operate like a privately held team whose external billionaire owners can withdraw dividends from the business. Its financial model instead directs available surpluses back towards football operations, stadium development and other club projects, although the cost of maintaining both the squad and the Bernabéu means that strong revenue must be sustained.Not all of Madrid's broader activity is designed to generate commercial returns, with the Real Madrid Foundation operating social and educational programmes through football and basketball across the world.The foundation, which marks 28 years of operations in 2025, runs more than 425 social sports schools across 102 countries and reports a global reach approaching two million people. Its programmes include more than 30,000 vulnerable young people, with over 14,000 beneficiaries across the Americas, while the 2025-26 season recorded its highest participation in national programmes for people with disabilities, including sensory schools and wheelchair-adapted basketball clinics.The foundation works through a mix of corporate partnerships, fundraising events, coaching programmes, in-kind donations and financial support from the club. Its annual funding is estimated at €18 million to €22 million ($20.9 million-$25.5 million), with approximately €15 million to €16 million ($17.4 million-$18.6 million) spent on ongoing social projects during 2025-26.Partners including Endesa, HSBC, UPS, GSK, Corpay and El Corte Inglés support specific programmes, while the annual Corazón Classic Match brings legends back to the Bernabéu to raise money through tickets, broadcasting and merchandise. The foundation also uses coaching clinics and educational congresses to generate income for projects that subsidise free sports schools in less affluent regions.During the latest season, programmes supported more than 1,515 children across the Middle East and over 3,200 across Asia-Pacific, including India, while adapted sports projects in Spain reached more than 700 beneficiaries. Partnerships with HP and Abbott also supported digital literacy, gender inclusion, health monitoring and nutrition initiatives, particularly in India and Indonesia.The foundation's emergency work included a €1 million ($1.16 million) club donation for earthquake relief in Venezuela in June 2026, matched by a further €1 million from president Florentino Pérez personally, bringing the reported contribution to €2 million ($2.32 million). In September, the club also formalised a partnership with the Community of Madrid's Ministry of Health to support people affected by rare diseases, particularly epidermolysis bullosa, commonly known as Butterfly Skin.Madrid's financial success extends beyond the headline revenue number, supporting a major sporting operation, an increasingly commercial stadium and a substantial social programme. The club has crossed a historic threshold, but sustaining that position will require its commercial growth to keep pace with the costs of its squad, its ambitious home and its wider commitments.
Article Summary: Real Madrid generated €1.221 billion ($1.42 billion) in operating revenue, becoming the first organisation in sports history to cross the €1 billion mark. The record comes despite an ambitious renovation of the Santiago Bernabéu, hefty investments in star players and a trophyless campaign. Real Madrid's operating revenue excludes player transfer fees, distinguishing the figure from financial measures that include income generated by selling footballers.

Article Title: Brazil forward who played against India handed four-match ban by Spanish football; here's why
Article Text:
UEFA Champions League - AS Roma v Real Madrid - Stadio Olimpico, Rome, Italy - October 14, 2026. Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior looks dejected after AS Roma's Donyell Malen scores their second goal

Mourinho blasts 'shameless' timing of ban

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr will miss the first Clasico of the season against Barcelona after the Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary committee handed him a four-match suspension on Wednesday.Vinicius was sent off during Real's 1-0 win over Villarreal on Saturday after pulling Nathan Saliba's hair shortly after coming on as a substitute. According to the disciplinary report for the eighth round of LaLiga fixtures, the committee handed him a two-match ban for the red-card offence and added another two matches for protesting to the referee.Vinicius was part of the Brazilian squad which defeated India 4-0 in the friendly match earlier this month in Kolkata.The suspension rules Vinicius out of league games against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander and Valencia. Real manager Jose Mourinho will therefore be without one of his forwards for the trip to Camp Nou on October 25.Vinicius has started all but one of Real's matches this season. He apologised to his teammates and Real Madrid fans on social media after the incident.The Clasico comes at an important stage of the title race, with Barcelona leading Real by six points in the league standings.Mourinho criticised the timing of the announcement, which came just hours before Real's Champions League match against Roma on Wednesday. The suspension will keep Vinicius out of a key run of league fixtures, including the Clasico against Barcelona.Vinicius started as Real produced a late comeback to beat Roma 4-3 in the Champions League. Mourinho's side had trailed 3-1 with seven minutes remaining before turning the match around.Speaking at his post-match press conference, Mourinho questioned why the decision had been announced so close to kick-off, saying it had disrupted the team's preparations.Mourinho said: "Do you think it's normal that a player from a Spanish team, who has to play a match that is also important for Spanish football, that two hours before the match a player knows he's been given a four-match suspension?"Couldn't they do it now? Couldn't they do it tomorrow morning? Do we have to come by bus and almost arrive at the stadium when we find out Vinicius has a four-match suspension?"Mourinho added: "They do things shamelessly now. The cat is out of the bag now. Two hours before the match, a player must know he has a four-match suspension."
Article Summary: Vinicius was sent off during Real's 1-0 win over Villarreal on Saturday. He pulled Nathan Saliba's hair shortly after coming on as a substitute. The suspension rules him out of league games against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander and Valencia. Jose Mourinho blasts'shameless' timing of ban.

Article Title: Barcelona's Lamine Yamal surpasses Kylian Mbappe as youngest ever to reach UCL milestone
Article Text:
Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe

Yamal’s dribble steals the show

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A record-breaking young Talent

Barcelona youngester Lamine Yamal has broken Kylian Mbappe ’s record to become the youngest player to reach 25 goal contributions in UEFA Champions League history. The 19-year-old achieved the milestone during Barcelona’s 4-1 comeback victory over Galatasaray, providing two assists in the match.Yamal set up Fermín’s goal in the 50th minute before assisting Anthony Gordon three minutes later.With this performance, he took his Champions League tally to 12 goals and 14 assists, reaching 25 goal contributions at the age of 19 years and 92 days. Mbappe previously held the record, having achieved the feat at 20 years and 306 days.Although Gordon scored Barcelona’s third goal, Yamal grabbed attention with an impressive dribble that created the scoring opportunity. After receiving the ball on the right side outside the penalty area, he used a step-over before pulling off a clever fake “rabona” to get past Galatasaray defender Eren Elmali. He then passed the ball to Gordon, who scored from close range.A rabona is a football move in which a player swings one leg behind the other to kick the ball. Yamal used a variation of the trick to beat his opponent and create space for the pass. Elmali appeared momentarily caught off guard by the move.Yamal described it as a “near-rabona” and explained his thinking after the match.“I've noticed lately that defenders have been diving to the ground whenever I make a run toward the backline,” Yamal said in a post-match interview with CBS Sports. “I saw an opportunity to pull off the move, which looks good but is also effective. I'm happy with it. I'm always trying to refine my dribbles to create more space. Defenders are always trying to close you down, so any kind of dribble that creates space is a lifesaver.After Gordon scored, several Barcelona players celebrated with the England forward, while others rushed to embrace Yamal.“He always surprises you,” Barcelona midfielder Rodri said.Yamal has also enjoyed an impressive season, recording 12 goals and 10 assists in 14 appearances for club and country. His Champions League achievement puts him ahead of Mbappe, Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham and Lionel Messi, highlighting his rapid rise among football’s biggest young stars.
Article Summary: Lamine Yamal has become the youngest player to reach 25 Champions League goals. The 19-year-old achieved the milestone during Barcelona’s 4-1 comeback victory over Galatasaray. Yamal set up Fermín and Gordon for the goals in the match.

Article Title: ISL: Raphael Eric Messi Bouli's late winner helps Punjab FC beat Odisha in thriller
Article Text:
Raphael Eric Messi Bouli (Image credit: ISL)

NEW DELHI: Punjab FC and Odisha FC delivered a dramatic start to their 2026–27 Indian Super League campaign, with Punjab edging a thrilling contest 2–1 at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium thanks to a 90+6 minute strike from Raphael Eric Messi Bouli.The result gave Punjab a memorable victory and left Odisha heartbroken .Punjab made an explosive start, with Messi Bouli finding the net in the first minute after an assist from Muhammed Uvais.The early breakthrough gave the hosts, coached by Pavlos Dermitzakis, momentum and put Odisha under pressure.Odisha visitors responded impressively, with Thoiba Singh Moirangthem scoring in the 15th minute following an assist from Lalthathanga Khawlhring.The second half became a test of patience and discipline. Both teams searched for a decisive breakthrough. Just when a draw appeared likely, Messi Bouli struck again to complete his brace and send Punjab into celebration.
Article Summary: Raphael Eric Messi Bouli scores twice to give Punjab 2-1 win over Odisha. Thoiba Singh Moirangthem had given Odisha the lead in the 15th minute. Punjab will play in the 2026–27 Indian Super League season.
